solution: Every channel that is actually used costs E_ij to activate plus L to push the program across it, so give each edge weight E_ij + L; the set of used channels must connect every station to some pre-installed station, and a cheapest such set is a spanning forest of the graph in which the S initial stations are contracted to a single vertex. Run Kruskal with union-find after pre-uniting the S sources, summing the accepted weights. The network is connected, so exactly N-S accepted edges (post-contraction, N-1 unions minus the S-1 free ones) always exist. O(M log M) time, O(N+M) space with M up to 10^6.
statement_summary: Stations form a connected weighted network; activating the channel between two stations costs a given amount, and afterwards transmitting the L-byte program across it costs L more. The program starts installed on S given stations and must reach every station. The task is the minimum total energy, with up to 10^4 stations and 10^6 channels.
notes: Sample (37) reproduced; brute force over all edge subsets agrees on 300 random connected graphs with up to 6 nodes and random source sets. Any MST algorithm works; Kruskal is just the convenient one for merging the sources first.
